reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness. HEAD remained unchanged. The Windows archive test step passed on the preceding commit, whose only difference from the reviewed HEAD is a task checkbox. Delivery can still accept invalid input or lose a model unit, and the interactive JSON and rollback diagnostics do not meet the committed contracts.
findings: CRITICAL — G1: Delivery accepts malformed Section operations. The Change requires rejecting empty operation blocks and RENAMED sections (`.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:17-25`). Archive uses only the compiler (`src/core/change-sync.ts:41-55`), whose Delta parser checks header presence but neither requires entries under a present header nor consumes `unsupportedSections` (`src/core/model/delta.ts:102-111`, `src/core/parsers/section-blocks.ts:123-142`). A read-only run of the committed code accepted an empty `## MODIFIED Sections` block as a no-op, which archive then moves into delivery history (`src/core/archive.ts:156-167`). A RENAMED block alongside a recognized block can likewise be ignored. The separate notation validator catches these cases but is not called by archive (`src/core/validation/validator.ts:39-58,94-99`).

CRITICAL — G1/G2: A nonempty Delta can bootstrap a missing Formal model, although the contract requires delivery to reject it (`.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:23-25`). Missing model partitions become an empty snapshot (`src/core/model/transaction.ts:297-319`); preparation validates the post-Delta model without requiring a Formal baseline (`src/core/change-sync.ts:41-55`, `src/core/change-compiler.ts:150-162`). A read-only run with a Delta adding a root Kind and root Element produced a writable manifest instead of rejecting delivery. The existing missing-model test uses no actual Delta and does not detect this case (`test/commands/output.test.ts:32-44`).

CRITICAL — G2/G5: Target-path collision detection is case-sensitive even on a case-insensitive filesystem. The writer treats `Foo.md` and `foo.md` as different claims (`src/core/model/sync-writer.ts:28-51`), and the transaction checks both preimages before either write, then installs both paths (`src/core/model/transaction.ts:271-284,362-398`). In a read-only simulation using case-insensitive lookup, a valid Delta adding `Foo` and `foo` through distinct input filenames prepared two writes, succeeded, and left only one unit. This violates the requirement to reject actual destination collisions before writing (`.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:23-25,39-41`). The existing collision test covers only identical path strings (`test/core/model/sync-writer.test.ts:207-236`).

CRITICAL — G2: The CLI drops compensation errors that the design requires it to report (`.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:15`). A failed staged-copy cleanup silently discards the cleanup error; a failed source restoration embeds the original and compensation errors in an `AggregateError` (`src/core/archive.ts:40-60`). Model rollback likewise stores compensation failures only in the aggregate (`src/core/model/transaction.ts:284-293`). The CLI prints only the outer `message`, so neither text nor JSON exposes the full failure causes (`src/cli/index.ts:192-198`).

CRITICAL — G1/G3/G5: Interactive `--json` puts prompt text and terminal control sequences on the same stdout stream as the JSON receipt. Archive uses Inquirer's default output for selection and confirmation (`src/core/change-utils.ts:41-45`, `src/core/archive.ts:97-100,111-113,137-147,158-164`), while the generated skill explicitly instructs callers to combine `--json` with CLI-managed confirmation (`.pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md:27-41`). A read-only probe of the pinned prompt dependency captured ANSI prompt output before the JSON object. This breaks the documented machine-readable output contract (`docs/cli.md:338-340`). The JSON abandonment test passes `--yes` and does not exercise the affected path (`test/commands/output.test.ts:108-122`).

CRITICAL — G3/G4: The generated Archive workflow can require readable Quality evidence before reaching abandonment. With no name supplied it directs the Agent to run `xirang list --json` before the abandonment branch (`src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:140-144`, `.pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md:24-28`). That listing reads Quality for every active Change before printing its result, and a malformed record throws (`src/core/list.ts:25-31,93-97,133-147`, `src/core/quality/engine.ts:321-332,130-146`). A malformed record on even an unrelated Change can therefore block the prescribed selection path. Abandonment is required to precede Quality reads and to work at any implementation stage (`.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:13`, `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/archive-role.md:13-19`).

CRITICAL — G2 verification: The design requires evidence that a failed receipt does not undo a committed delivery (`.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:15,25-27`). The retry tests either pre-create history or retry after a successful call (`test/commands/output.test.ts:23-30,108-122`, `test/core/archive-branch-merge.test.ts:174-188`). They would still pass if a receipt failure rolled back the model or directory move. `git grep -n -Ei 'lost receipt|receipt lost|lost.*response|response.*lost|stdout.*(EPIPE|throw|fail)|output.*(EPIPE|throws)' HEAD -- test` found no receipt-failure test; its sole match was an unrelated JSON parsing assertion. Add a fault-injection test at the receipt boundary that verifies both model and archive stay committed and retry reports the existing result.

reviews.summary: Reviewed Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness across the cumulative Change. HEAD remained unchanged. All 165 targeted committed tests passed on Linux, but independent probes reproduced invalid Delta delivery, a mismatch between the applied and archived Delta, destination replacement, and fallback artifact damage.
findings: CRITICAL — Delivery can archive and write a Delta that `validate --change --preview` rejects. `prepareChangeSync` uses compiler diagnostics but omits the Section-notation checks performed by the standalone validator. I reproduced quick delivery of a heading-only `ADDED` Section: preview reported missing Section text, but archive wrote the empty Section to Formal and moved the Change. A separate probe showed that an empty `ADDED Sections` block followed by a second block of the same name is silently discarded before the empty-block check. This violates G1 and the empty-block Required Correction. See `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/tasks.md:3-5,19-21`, `src/core/change-sync.ts:41-59`, `src/commands/validate.ts:199-221`, `src/core/validation/validator.ts:165-186`, `src/core/parsers/section-blocks.ts:123-161`, and `src/core/model/delta.ts:102-120`.

CRITICAL — Delivery can apply one Delta and archive a different one. `archive` prepares the manifest before the task confirmation, rechecks only Formal, then moves the live Change directory. In a probe that edited a Delta unit during the confirmation prompt, the command returned success: Formal contained the old target and the archive contained the new target. Bind the Delta being moved to the prepared input, rejecting drift without delivery. See `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:13-15`, `src/core/archive.ts:137-145,162-173`, `src/core/change-sync.ts:41-64,85-99`, and `src/core/model/transaction.ts:264-285`.

CRITICAL — The destination no-overwrite guarantee is not enforced at installation. The existence check and rename are separate operations; both the direct and staged rename can replace a destination that appears in between. On Linux I reproduced successful abandonment replacing an empty destination created after the check. The existing collision test only covers a destination present before the call. See `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:15-16`, `src/core/archive.ts:33-44,127-140`, and `test/core/archive.test.ts:434-446`.

CRITICAL — Cross-device fallback does not preserve a Change unchanged. Both copies use `fs.cp` without `verbatimSymlinks`. In a probe, forced `EXDEV` converted an internal relative artifact link into an absolute link to the old active path, then deleted that path and reported success. The existing fallback tests use only regular files. See `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-archive.md:15-23,55-57`, `src/core/archive.ts:40-64`, and `test/integration/archive-workflow.test.ts:17-75`.

CRITICAL — The managed quick workflow can still be blocked by Quality before archive runs. An unnamed quick request uses `xirang list --json`, which reads Quality for all active Changes; a malformed or unsupported record rejects the list, even if it belongs to an unrelated Change. The generated workflow also unconditionally enters Git handoff after successful quick delivery, despite the retained non-Git contract requiring it to report the result without attempting Git operations. See `src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:140-163`, `.pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md:24-49`, `src/core/list.ts:24-31,90-99`, `src/core/quality/engine.ts:130-149`, and `.xirang/model/elements/change-archive.md:220-224`.

CRITICAL — Seal failures lack the required route back to Apply. The CLI returns a generic message for missing Seal or forwards the underlying error; the generated workflow neither directs the user back to Apply nor obtains the Quality status that its Git handoff says it retained. The adjacent `formatQualityGateFailure` now suggests retrying archive but is orphaned: `git grep -n -E 'formatQualityGateFailure' HEAD -- src test` found only its definition and direct unit tests, with no production caller. See `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/agent-prompt-guidance.md:24-28`, `src/core/archive.ts:156-161`, `src/cli/index.ts:192-199`, `src/core/quality/state.ts:24-51`, and `src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:146-160`.

CRITICAL — The conflicting options are rejected inside the archive action, not at parse time as Design Decision 1 requires. Commander has already run the pre-action hooks when `ArchiveCommand.execute` checks the flags. The current test asserts only the exit code, message, and active path, so it cannot distinguish the required parse-time rejection from the current behavior. See `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:13`, `src/cli/index.ts:69-85,186-199`, `src/core/archive.ts:90-94`, and `test/commands/output.test.ts:109-122`.

CRITICAL — Two required confirmation guarantees lack mutation-sensitive tests. The quick-decline test has no pending Delta, so it would still pass if model writes occurred before confirmation. The abandonment test checks `2/5` only on the declined invocation and does not check its order relative to the prompt or reassert it under `--yes`. Add assertions that declining preserves a genuinely pending model target and that `--yes` still emits progress without prompting. See `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-archive.md:35-41`, `test/core/archive.test.ts:234-254,525-571`; `git grep -nEi 'stale.*(archive|confirm)|delta.*(during|after).*confirm' HEAD -- test` returned no additional matches.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness. HEAD remained unchanged. Four defects block approval: a losing delivery can undo a successful delivery, Archive can validate against a model the normal reader cannot see, fallback rollback can fail on an unchanged symlink, and a retry can return the wrong archive.
findings: CRITICAL — A losing delivery can undo a successful one. The formal fingerprint and preimages are checked before the writes, and rollback restores them unconditionally (src/core/model/transaction.ts:264–294, 409–428). The destination is reserved only after those writes (src/core/archive.ts:51–56, 212–219). Two deliveries of the same Change can both pass the prechecks; if one finishes before the other resumes writing, the loser then detects the missing active Delta and rolls back the winner's model update. The winner has already returned success and its archive remains. This violates design.md:14–16. The collision test creates only an empty destination, not a competing committed delivery (test/core/archive.test.ts:453–469); `git grep -n -Ei 'concurrent|race|winner|stale'` over the archive and sync tests found no test exercising two deliveries.

CRITICAL — Archive can deliver a target that ordinary Formal readers reject. Archive parses the transaction tree after filtering hidden paths (src/core/change-sync.ts:44–55). That tree reads symlink targets as files (src/core/model/transaction.ts:297–319), but ordinary Formal loading skips symlink entries (src/core/change-compiler.ts:51–53; src/core/model/parser.ts:394–426). For example, Archive can accept a new element whose parent exists only through a symlink in `elements/`, then report success even though ordinary Formal loading cannot resolve that parent. This violates the same-Formal-snapshot and target-integrity requirements in .xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:17–25. `git grep -n -Ei 'symlink|symbolic link|dangling link'` over the model, sync, and archive tests found only the archive artifact-link test (test/integration/archive-workflow.test.ts:37–47).

CRITICAL — Cross-device rollback can fail on a symlink that cleanup never removed. After a partial failure deleting the active source, the fallback copies the entire destination over the surviving source with `force: true` and `verbatimSymlinks: true` (src/core/archive.ts:34–37, 89–99). Node 22's `fs.cp` rejects copying an absolute symlink over a surviving symlink to the same target; `force` does not override that check. A recoverable deletion failure can therefore leave both the installed archive and a partially deleted active Change. This fails the rollback guarantee in design.md:15 and the symlink correction in tasks.md:31. The success test covers only a relative link, and the rollback test has no symlink and replaces `cp` with a wrapper that drops the production copy options (test/integration/archive-workflow.test.ts:37–47, 83–112).

CRITICAL — A lost abandonment receipt can resolve to a different, delivered Change. `new change` permits name reuse once the active directory is gone (src/commands/workflow/new-change.ts:25–42; src/utils/change-utils.ts:133–149). Archive permits same-day delivered and abandoned records for that name at separate destinations, but retry lookup combines both outcomes, ignores the requested mode, and sorts by date/name alone, with the delivered entry first on a tie (src/core/archive.ts:104–113, 152–171). Deliver a Change, reuse its name and abandon it later the same day: retrying `--abandon` returns the earlier delivery's path. This fails the lost-receipt behavior in .xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-archive.md:51–53 and G5 in tasks.md:15–17. The lookup tests cover a single exact match or a different-name suffix, not both outcomes for the exact same name (test/commands/output.test.ts:40–47, 125–140; confirmed by `git grep -n -Ei 'abandoned|alreadyArchived'` over the archive and CLI output tests).

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change across Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness. The three modes and CLI retirement are present, but delivery can lose a concurrent Formal update or a late Delta edit, accept an invalid Section, and report success without installing a readable Formal unit. HEAD and worktree status were unchanged during review.
findings: CRITICAL — A failed delivery can erase another Change's successful Formal update. Archive reserves only its own dated destination (`src/core/archive.ts:64-69,193-205,244-253`). Different Changes can both pass the same Formal fingerprint and preimage checks before either writes; the slower one can then overwrite the winner and restore the obsolete preimage if its move fails (`src/core/model/transaction.ts:265-294,417-435`). A pinned in-memory probe observed `winning update` revert to `before`. This violates the stale-baseline and rollback guarantees in `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:23-37`. The contention test uses the same Change and destination (`test/core/archive.test.ts:472-507`), so it does not catch this case.

CRITICAL — The copy fallback can close the same active Change as both delivered and abandoned. The two modes reserve different destinations (`src/core/archive.ts:193-219`); each can stage the same source, and both can finish because forced source removal also succeeds once the other invocation has removed it (`src/core/archive.ts:36-39,64-87,105-121`). A pinned in-memory probe produced both histories from one active directory. This violates the distinct outcomes in `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-archive.md:17-23`.

CRITICAL — A Delta edit can be lost after fallback verification but before the move commits. The fallback verifies its staged destination and active source, then separately removes the active source (`src/core/archive.ts:77-87,105-116,242-253`). A pinned in-memory probe changed the source at that boundary: the command succeeded with the old Delta in history and deleted the edit. This violates the required correction in `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/tasks.md:28-29`. Existing drift tests cover confirmation and same-device rename, not fallback source removal (`test/core/archive.test.ts:666-697`).

CRITICAL — Empty Section bodies bypass archive validation when an Element Declaration is stored outside `elements/`. The compiler dispatches by declared entity (`src/core/model/delta.ts:102-134`), but the notation pass filters the snapshot by filename partition (`src/core/change-sync.ts:51-65`; `src/core/validation/validator.ts:165-185,223-230`). The notation explicitly says a partition does not determine entity type (`.xirang/references/xirang-model-notation.md:4-11`). A pinned probe showed both gates accept an empty Section on an optional-contract Element stored under `views/`. The existing empty-body test only uses `elements/` (`test/core/archive.test.ts:269-283`).

CRITICAL — Delivery can report success for an added unit that the Formal reader cannot see. `.hidden` is a valid identity (`src/core/model/validator.ts:10,23-33`); a visible Delta file declaring it is compiled into `elements/.hidden.md` (`src/core/model/sync-writer.ts:67-81`), which the Formal reader skips (`src/core/model/parser.ts:394-413`). The transaction does not check that the persisted Formal model matches the validated target before moving the Change (`src/core/model/transaction.ts:272-285`; `src/core/archive.ts:244-256`). A pinned probe confirmed that compilation and notation passed but a Formal reread omitted the new Element. This violates `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:17-25`.

CRITICAL — The current getting-started walkthrough still teaches users that Archive runs Review and Opt when evidence is missing (`docs/getting-started.md:207-217`). The actual workflow stops and returns the user to Apply (`src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:146-157`), as required by `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/archive-quality-gate.md:13-23`. Update the walkthrough to show the real recovery path.

CRITICAL — No persistent test proves that default Archive rejects a structurally valid Seal whose commit no longer resolves, preserves state, and reports the specific failure with an Apply handoff (`src/core/archive.ts:223-233`; `src/core/quality/engine.ts:194-201,341-345`). `git grep -n -E 'readQualitySeal|GIT_COMMIT_NOT_FOUND|MALFORMED_QUALITY_RECORD|UNSUPPORTED_QUALITY_VERSION' HEAD -- test` found no such Archive case: the missing-object assertion records a Review (`test/commands/quality.test.ts:109-114`), and the Seal reader test rejects invalid fields (`test/core/quality/engine.test.ts:272-291`). The archive tests cover no Seal and valid Seals (`test/core/archive.test.ts:171-218`); those cases would still pass if Archive stopped resolving the stored Seal commit.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness. HEAD did not move. Two transaction defects were reproduced in memory; current guidance also contradicts the new archive protocol, and the destination-race test does not verify the required ordering.
findings: CRITICAL — Legal leading-dot identities cannot be delivered for Element Kinds, Relationship Kinds, or Authored Views. The identity validator accepts them (`src/core/model/validator.ts:10–33`), but the writer only escapes leading dots for Element and relationship-container filenames (`src/core/model/sync-writer.ts:41–43,80–106`). The ordinary Formal reader skips the resulting Kind and View files, so delivery rolls back instead of sealing (`src/core/model/parser.ts:395–413`; `src/core/change-sync.ts:110–118`). An in-memory run reproduced all three failures; the regression test covers only an Element (`test/core/archive.test.ts:339–347`). This leaves Required Correction 43 incomplete.

CRITICAL — A failed delivery can destroy unrelated pre-existing bytes at a staging pathname. The Formal snapshot excludes hidden files (`src/core/model/parser.ts:395–413`), but the transaction writes to a predictable hidden filename without exclusively creating it, then renames or removes it. Rollback restores only manifest destinations (`src/core/model/transaction.ts:383–435`). An in-memory run with pre-existing bytes at that pathname and a simulated move failure restored the model unit but lost the unrelated file. Use an exclusively created staging file and test that a pre-existing file is preserved.

CRITICAL — Current documentation and generated guidance disagree with the closure contract. `docs/cli.md:53` still says Archive requires a synchronized Delta and a Seal, contradicting its own mode-specific instructions at lines 328–341. The workflow registry still describes Archive as completed-change-only, and the common skill projects that description (`src/core/templates/manifest/registry.ts:60–70`; `src/core/templates/workflows/common.ts:21–24`; `.pi/skills/xirang-common/SKILL.md:31–36`). The schema and installed reference also tell Agents not to archive `.delta-noop`, which conflicts with the requirement to move the Change unchanged (`schemas/semantic-model/schema.yaml:58–61`; `.xirang/references/xirang-artifact-semantic-delta.md:24–26`; `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-archive.md:13–23`). Update the source guidance and its managed projection, not the preserved Change contents.

CRITICAL — The destination-race regression test does not prove that reservation precedes Formal writes. The implementation reserves before applying (`src/core/archive.ts:66–71,131–139`), but the race fixture inserts the winner during `mkdir` and checks Formal bytes only after failure (`test/core/archive.test.ts:517–534`). A regression that writes Formal first and then rolls it back on collision would still pass. The committed test search for destination-reservation ordering found no other assertion at that boundary. Assert that Formal is still unchanged when the competing destination appears.

reviews.summary: 已审查完整累计 Change 的完整性、正确性、一致性与整洁性，审查期间 HEAD 未变。196 项现有聚焦测试通过，但独立复现发现：默认交付可使用已撤销的 Seal，跨设备归档可在活动 Delta 被重建后仍交付旧目标，非法 Section operation 可被静默丢弃。另有一项确认行为缺少有效的回归断言。
findings: CRITICAL — 默认交付可在 Seal 被撤销后写入 Formal。归档在任务确认前读取 Seal，确认后的提交路径只复查 Delta，不复查 Quality（`src/core/archive.ts:278–309`）。独立复现中，在确认期间通过正式 Quality Review API 记录 FAIL，API 将 Seal 清空（`src/core/quality/engine.ts:204–222`）；归档仍更新 Formal，并封存了 `seal: null` 的记录。违反 `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/archive-quality-gate.md:17–23`。应在提交窗口重新核实实际交付所消费的 Seal，并覆盖确认期间 Seal 失效时不写 Formal、不移动 Change 的回归用例。

CRITICAL — 跨设备复制期间重建活动 Delta 时，归档仍报告旧目标交付成功。源目录被移入临时位置后，代码只复查暂存源与归档目标，从未检查原活动路径是否重现（`src/core/archive.ts:89–109,251–262`）。独立复现中，复制期间在原路径重建了含新 Delta 的活动目录；命令仍返回新归档回执，Formal 和归档均保留旧 Delta，而同名 Change 仍处于活动状态。违反 `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-archive.md:13–23` 和 `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/tasks.md:29,41`。现有测试实际在移动到暂存源之前编辑（`test/core/archive.test.ts:790–821`），没有覆盖暂存后的竞争。修复时不得覆盖重建目录或删除任何一份输入。

CRITICAL — 交付可静默丢弃非法 Section operation。`parseDeltaSpec` 只取三个已知块，并只把 `RENAMED Sections` 识别为不支持；编译与归档记法校验都采用这份结果（`src/core/parsers/section-blocks.ts:124–151`、`src/core/model/delta.ts:102–123`、`src/core/validation/validator.ts:44–69`）。独立复现中，合法 `ADDED Sections` 旁的 `DELETED Sections` 未产生诊断；quick 成功归档，Formal 只反映合法块。违反 `.xirang/model/elements/semantic-delta.md:43–69` 及 `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:17–25`。应拒绝混合有效与非法 operation 的输入，并断言 Formal 与活动目录保持不变。

CRITICAL — 缺少 `tasks.md` 时不应询问，但现有回归用例无法检出错误询问。`test/core/archive.test.ts:627–640` 传入 `--yes` 并检查 stdout，而真正的确认与警告分别走 `confirm` 和 stderr（`src/core/archive.ts:264–269,292–298`）。如果回归为总是进入未完成任务分支，该测试仍可通过。`git grep -niE 'without tasks|missing tasks|no tasks|no goals' HEAD -- test/core/archive.test.ts test/core/archive-branch-merge.test.ts test/commands/output.test.ts test/integration/archive-workflow.test.ts` 只找到这个用例。应在不传 `--yes` 的情况下断言未调用确认且完成归档，以覆盖 `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-archive.md:19–22`。

WARNING — `src/core/completions/positional-types.ts:11–20` 仍保留已退役的 `sync` positional metadata。补全从实际注册的命令树生成（`src/core/completions/introspect.ts:24–38,80–85`）；独立检查确认当前 help 和 Bash 补全未暴露旧用法。建议删除这条无效映射，避免维护者误以为命令仍被支持。

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness at an unchanged HEAD. Confirmed three blockers: late source recreation can escape rollback, archive fallback can delete independently written destination data, and validation can silently discard an unscoped Section.
findings: CRITICAL — Recreating the active Change during cross-device source cleanup still commits delivery. `src/core/archive.ts:114-119` checks whether the active path exists, then awaits deletion of the detached original without checking again. An in-memory run of the committed Archive and model transaction recreated the Change during that deletion and observed a success receipt, the updated Formal model, the archive, and the new active Change. This violates `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:15` and `tasks.md:51`. The existing regression at `test/core/archive.test.ts:874-905` recreates the path during copy, before the last check; add coverage for recreation during cleanup.

CRITICAL — A destination populated after reservation can be deleted by fallback compensation. `src/core/archive.ts:60-75` treats `ENOTEMPTY` as a fallback signal even after reserving the target. If fallback copy then encounters an independently written destination file, `src/core/archive.ts:107-110,121-139` recursively removes the entire destination, including that file. An in-memory run of the committed mover reproduced the deletion. This violates the no-overwrite decisions in `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:15-16`. `test/core/archive.test.ts:553-570` protects a destination created before reservation, not one populated after it; add a regression that checks the independent bytes survive.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness. Two read-only checks reproduced semantic or artifact loss. The generated Archive workflow also imposes a stricter Quality gate than the CLI, and the getting-started guide shows Delta syntax that Archive rejects. HEAD was unchanged.
findings: CRITICAL — Delivery can silently drop an untouched Section. The post-write check compares installed bytes to the prepared serialization rather than comparing the model obtained by parsing those bytes to the Expected Semantic Model (src/core/change-sync.ts:64–75,105–122). In a read-only check against committed source, a MODIFIED Section with normative prose followed by an unclosed code fence passed compilation and notation validation. The compiled target contained [First, Untouched], but the ordinary Formal parser returned [First] with no diagnostics: serialization put Untouched inside the open fence (src/core/model/serializer.ts:16–28; src/core/parsers/section-blocks.ts:32–37,63–95). This violates the target-integrity requirement in .xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:17–25. The existing guard test substitutes a wrong fingerprint rather than exercising a readable byte image with the wrong semantics (test/integration/sync-workflow.test.ts:99–108).

CRITICAL — File edits can be lost during source cleanup in both delivery and abandonment. The last content fingerprint is checked before deleting the captured source. After deletion, Archive checks destination ownership and whether the active pathname was recreated, then clears the pending marker without checking for a file edit to the captured source during cleanup (src/core/archive.ts:195–214,401–444). An in-memory filesystem check against the committed mover injected a successful ordinary-file edit immediately inside source cleanup, without replacing any directory. Archive returned success with the stale bytes and retained no copy of the edit. The existing tests cover an edit during destination copy and directory recreation during cleanup, not a file edit during cleanup (test/core/archive.test.ts:590–614,1064–1101). This violates the late-edit preservation correction in .xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/tasks.md:63–64.

CRITICAL — The generated default Archive workflow reopens Review and Opt eligibility instead of consuming only a valid Seal. The template and installed skill require passing Review states and an Opt disposition before allowing the Archive call, and invoke `quality status`, which recomputes post-Opt ancestry (src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:149–157; .pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md:33–41; src/commands/quality.ts:72–82; src/core/quality/engine.ts:280–303,325–352). A valid sealed record can therefore be rejected by the workflow if a different reviewed commit used in that ancestry check is no longer resolvable, even though the Seal commit still exists and the Archive CLI accepts it. That extra gate contradicts .xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/archive-quality-gate.md:13–23. The template test checks for the status command and Apply handoff text, not agreement with the CLI gate (test/core/templates/archive-change.test.ts:41–47).

CRITICAL — The current getting-started guide tells users to put explanatory prose beneath a REMOVED Section, then presents the Delta as ready to archive (docs/getting-started.md:76–114). The new parser treats that exact prose as unexpected REMOVED content and rejects the delivery, as the archive regression test confirms (src/core/parsers/section-blocks.ts:187–197; src/core/model/delta.ts:104–108; test/core/archive.test.ts:330–342). Update the example to show a title-only removal so the documented workflow works with the delivered protocol.

findings: CRITICAL — A write through an already-open artifact handle can be lost before commit. `src/core/archive.ts:217-234` fingerprints the parked originals, then performs more asynchronous filesystem operations before removing the `.pending` marker. `src/core/archive.ts:273-278` then deletes the parked originals. In an isolated probe, a write through the original `proposal.md` handle completed before marker removal, but the move succeeded with the old bytes and deleted the only copy of the edit. This violates the full-snapshot and late-write requirements in `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/tasks.md:64,73`, without any external directory replacement. `test/core/archive.test.ts:655-691` injects the write during captured-directory cleanup, before the last fingerprint, and does not cover this commit boundary.

An isolated probe made only that `lstat` fail with `EIO`; the empty destination and marker both remained even though cleanup was available. A subsequent active-Change invocation rejects the existing destination at `src/core/archive.ts:399-426`. This violates the compensation decision in `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/design.md:15`. `git grep -n -Ei 'post.?reservation.*lstat|lstat.*(reservation|owned destination)' HEAD -- test` returned no matches.

The committed discovery function returned a marked partial destination in an isolated probe. findings: CRITICAL — A REMOVED Section with Markdown closing hashes can be silently skipped. `### Section: Legacy behavior ###` becomes the literal identity `root#Legacy behavior ###`; the already-applied logic then accepts it as absent while `Legacy behavior` remains in Formal. An in-memory run of the committed parser and compiler confirmed that notation and compilation both pass, with no diagnostics and the original Section still present. This violates the normalized Section identity and invalid-notation requirements in `.xirang/changes/atomic-change-archive/elements/change-sync.md:17-25`. See `src/core/parsers/section-blocks.ts:21-28,246-269`, `src/core/change-compiler.ts:109-129`, and `src/core/change-sync.ts:65-86`. The archive tests cover hashes-only titles, not a real title followed by closing hashes (`test/core/archive.test.ts:321-345`).

The template tells the agent to run `xirang status` and ignore its Quality fields, but that command invokes Quality completion when the goals are complete. Quality completion evaluates Review results and post-Opt Git ancestry before returning. Ignoring the projection does not prevent these checks, contrary to Required Correction 63. See `src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:139-145`, `.pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md:30-36`, `src/commands/workflow/status.ts:54-60`, and `src/core/quality/engine.ts:292-303,325-342`. Its global Input rule says the agent MUST ask for the exact name when unspecified and ambiguous; the mode-specific rule says to use the Quality-independent interactive CLI selector and ask for the name only when no interactive terminal exists. An agent can follow the global rule and never reach the interactive route required by Required Correction 26. Scope the exact-name rule to delivery or noninteractive abandonment. See `src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:129-137,177-186`, `.pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md:20-28`, and `test/core/templates/archive-change.test.ts:34-39`, which checks the command is present but not that the routing is unambiguous.

reviews.summary: Reviewed Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness across the cumulative Change. HEAD remained unchanged. Delivery silently archives an invalid Delta, failed delivery can broaden Formal permissions, and the workflow index sends Snack users to the wrong archive mode.
findings: CRITICAL — Delivery silently discards declaration-only Delta units without an operation. The authoring contract permits omitting `operation` only for Section changes (`.xirang/references/xirang-artifact-semantic-delta.md:37–47`). `src/core/model/delta.ts:85–103` emits no entry or error for a declaration with an empty body and no operation, and `src/core/validation/validator.ts:235–241` skips that unit. The generated Archive workflow defaults to Seal-gated delivery and requires explicit authorization for quick (`src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:129–145`). WARNING — Archived-history discovery lists delivered history only. `src/utils/item-discovery.ts:40–63` scans the top-level archive directory, while retry lookup checks both outcomes (`src/core/archive.ts:161–179`).
